scenarios.title: {tyler} Gets Cut
scenarios.text: {tyler} is released on a Monday morning. He calls you before he calls his agent, and for a long time neither of you says anything.

choices.label: Listen for an hour
choices.result: An hour on the phone, mostly listening. He doesn't want advice, and you don't give any, and he thanks you twice.

choices.label: Make a call for him
choices.result: A special teams coach you know gets a call from you, and you say {tyler}'s name twice. He has a workout by Friday.

choices.label: Promise to talk soon
choices.result: A message, warm and short, and a promise to talk soon. You mean it, and it still takes three weeks before you actually call.

scenarios.title: The Holder's Last Season
scenarios.text: {holder} is retiring after this season and wants every hold to count. They've started bringing a notebook to practice, writing down each one, with the date and the weather.

choices.label: Celebrate every practice
choices.result: Every practice becomes a small celebration: a joke, a photo, a cake on the fortieth birthday. {holder} cries twice, happily.

choices.label: Make every kick count
choices.result: Every kick in practice, for {holder}, like it's the playoffs. The notebook fills up with good ones, and {holder} reads them to you on Fridays.

choices.label: Train the next holder
choices.result: The next holder gets trained by both of you, all season, so the job is in good hands. {holder} calls it the best thing you ever did for them.

scenarios.title: The Concussion
scenarios.text: A teammate who has had too many concussions takes another hit in practice and hides it. You saw it happen, and he saw you see it.

choices.label: Tell the trainers
choices.result: The trainers hear it from you before the next drill. He's angry for a week and won't look at you, then thanks you in the parking lot.

choices.label: Talk to him first
choices.result: Away from everyone, by the water cooler, you convince him to tell the trainers himself. It costs you an hour and some of his pride.

choices.label: Look the other way
choices.result: Looking the other way, you let it go. He plays the next game, and you watch him every single snap, wondering if you were wrong.

scenarios.title: A College Teammate's Wedding
scenarios.text: Your old college roommate is getting married in June and wants you to give the toast. He's sent a list of stories you're not allowed to tell, and it's longer than the speech.

choices.label: Write a great toast
choices.result: A great toast, written over three weeks and delivered from memory. The bride's grandmother hugs you twice, and the groom mouths 'thank you' from the head table.

choices.label: Tell one true story
choices.result: One true story from freshman year, carefully chosen. It's the one people repeat at breakfast the next morning, and the groom tears up.

choices.label: Remember the pact
choices.result: You raise a glass to the pact you made freshman year. He laughs so hard he can't finish his drink.
choices.lock_text: having made a pact with your college roommate

choices.label: Make peace in the toast
choices.result: You haven't really talked since college. You say so in the toast, and you say sorry. He finds you on the patio afterward.
choices.lock_text: having fallen out with your college roommate

scenarios.title: The Snapper Retires
scenarios.text: The long snapper you've trusted for years is done: his back, his age, his wife's patience. He asks you, of all people, to speak at his farewell dinner.

choices.label: Speak from the heart
choices.result: What it's like to trust someone without ever looking back: you tell the room. He cries first, and then everyone else does.

choices.label: Keep it light and true
choices.result: Three funny stories and one true one. The room loves it, and he asks for a copy of the speech to show his kids.

choices.label: Say a few words
choices.result: A few short words and a raised glass of water. He hugs you anyway, hard, and says it was perfect, and his wife writes you a note.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Who Can't Let Go
scenarios.text: A thirty-six-year-old linebacker is getting cut on Friday, and he hasn't figured it out yet. He's still planning next year's offseason out loud at lunch.

choices.label: Sit with him on his last day
choices.result: Lunch with him on his last day, just the two of you. He talks about his first season the whole time, and you let him.

choices.label: Get the young players to say goodbye
choices.result: The young players, quietly told to say goodbye before he's gone. Twenty of them line up at his locker, and he can't speak.

choices.label: Let it happen
choices.result: It's not your place, so you let it happen. It stays with you, the empty chair at lunch, longer than you expect.

scenarios.title: The Players-Only Meeting
scenarios.text: The team captains call a players-only meeting about {coach}'s boss, the head coach, and they want every player's vote. For the first time, they're asking the kicker.

choices.label: Speak honestly
choices.result: Tough and fair, you say about the head coach, and you give two examples. Some agree, some don't, and the vote is closer because of you.

choices.label: Ask for the facts first
choices.result: What exactly is the problem? The meeting gets calmer as people answer, and the vote becomes a list of fixes instead.

choices.label: Abstain
choices.result: An abstention. Kickers rarely get asked anyway, and you'd rather not start now. The captains notice, and they stop asking you for a while.

scenarios.title: The Player Rep
scenarios.text: The team needs a players' union representative, the job of standing up in front of management twice a year. Nobody wants to be the one management remembers.

choices.label: Volunteer
choices.result: Volunteered. It's meetings and conference calls, and the young players start coming to you with questions about everything from contracts to pensions.

choices.label: Nominate the right person
choices.result: The veteran who should do it gets nominated by you. He accepts, grumbling, and does it brilliantly for three years.

choices.label: Leave it to someone else
choices.result: Someone else does it. You vote for them and go back to kicking, relieved, a little guiltily, every time there's a meeting.

scenarios.title: The Injured Teammate
scenarios.text: A teammate who tore his knee for the team last season is cut the day he's cleared to practice. He found out in the training room, still wearing the brace.

choices.label: Help him clean out his locker
choices.result: His locker, cleaned out with your help, into two cardboard boxes. He doesn't say much, and he hugs you at the car.

choices.label: Say something to the room
choices.result: A few words to the room about how this business works and what we owe each other inside it. The young players listen closely.

choices.label: Keep quiet
choices.result: Quiet. You're one bad season from the same thing, and you know it, and you kick a little angrier that week.

scenarios.title: The Podcast
scenarios.text: A popular podcast wants you for a full hour. The host is famous for getting athletes to say too much, and three of your teammates have already regretted going on.

choices.label: Prepare and stay disciplined
choices.result: Prepared, disciplined, and still funny. It's a good episode with no headlines, and the host admits you were a hard interview.

choices.label: Be yourself on air
choices.result: Funny and honest for an hour, until one joke about a teammate gets clipped everywhere. You apologize to him before he hears it.

choices.label: Turn the podcast down
choices.result: No, politely. The host says something snide about kickers on the next episode, and your teammates send it to you, delighted.

scenarios.title: The National Deal
scenarios.text: A national brand wants you for a commercial that would air during every game this year: you, a ball, and a talking dog. The shoot is during your bye week.

choices.label: Sign on for the commercial
choices.result: Signed. You're on every broadcast all season, the talking dog becomes famous, and the shoot eats your entire bye week, which you never get back.

choices.label: Shoot it in the offseason
choices.result: The offseason, or nothing, you tell them politely. They agree, the dog waits, and your bye week stays your own, with your family.

choices.label: Pass on it
choices.result: No commercial this year. You'd rather be known for kicking than for the dog, and a punter gets the part instead and loves it.

scenarios.title: The Leak
scenarios.text: Someone is leaking locker-room conversations to a beat reporter, word for word, and the coaches think it's a specialist. The punter is furious. So is {holder}.

choices.label: Find the pattern
choices.result: Which details leak, and when? You notice the pattern and tell {coach}: it's a rookie lineman with a cousin at the paper.

choices.label: Rally the specialists
choices.result: The specialists, gathered: everyone knows what's at stake, and nobody says anything outside the room. {holder} calls it a team meeting.

choices.label: Let the coaches sort it
choices.result: The coaches will sort it out, you decide. They do, slowly, and the specialists' room stays tense and quiet for a month.

scenarios.title: The Prime Slump
scenarios.text: You're supposed to be at your best, and the misses in practice have started making headlines. The coaches haven't said anything about it yet, which is worse.

choices.label: Go back to the film
choices.result: You go back to the film of your best season and find the one thing that changed: your plant foot drifted half an inch. It takes a week to fix.

choices.label: Kick two hundred a day
choices.result: You kick through it, two hundred extra balls a day. Your leg aches, your rhythm comes back, and nobody can say you didn't work.

choices.label: Lean on the holder
choices.result: You and {holder} go back to basics together, laughing at how far you've come. It helps more than you expected.

choices.label: Use the tools you learned
choices.result: The tools you learned the last time this happened come right back: the breath, the word, the one thought. The slump is shorter this time, by a lot.
